title: Overlabels Recipe Manifest
description: Declarative description of a Recipe: the things it installs into an account (overlays, integration connections), the primitives it wires together (option sets, pickers), the controls it exports, and the triggers that fire its pickers. Manifests are 100% declarative - no executable code - because they are intended to be Claude-auditable before publishing.

recipe_format_version.description: The schema version this manifest targets. The installer rejects formats it does not understand.

slug.description: Globally unique identifier for the recipe, and the public URL at /products/<slug>. Hyphens for a listed product, so the URL reads as words. A recipe with control_exports must stay snake_case: its slug becomes part of the [[[c:<slug>:<instance>:<name>]]] tag namespace, and a control identifier never carries a dash.

version.description: Integer version. A new version is a new installable artifact, never an in-place upgrade.

description.description: Short blurb shown on the recipe's install page.

icon_url.description: URL to an icon image (PNG/JPG/WebP). Optional.

changelog.description: Notes on what changed in this version.

min_overlabels_version.description: Minimum platform schema version this manifest needs. Increments only on breaking changes to the recipe-format itself.

requires_integrations.description: List of external integration source keys this recipe reads controls from (e.g. ['kofi', 'streamlabs']). Installer warns but does not block when an installer lacks one of these.

max_instances_per_user.description: Per-user install cap for this recipe. Defaults to platform-wide admin setting if omitted.

url_aliases.description: Slugs this product used to live at. /products/<alias> answers 301 to the current slug, so a link written before a rename still lands. Never reused by another recipe.

listed.description: Whether the recipe is shown on the public /products page as an installable product. Unlisted recipes can still be installed by a seeder or tinker.

category.description: Which shelf of the /products page a listed recipe sits on. At most one, not hierarchical: `product` is something viewers do in chat and see on stream, `alert` is a service the streamer already uses landing on their stream. A listed recipe without one is shown after both shelves under Show all and under no filter. Optional.

requires_bot.description: Whether the installed result only works with the Overlabels bot in the streamer's chat. Drives the human steps on the product page: it is not something the installer can do.

hero.description: Site-relative path of a 16:9 hero image shown above the product on the /products listing. Lives under public/products/. Optional.

follower_pins.description: How many of the channel's followers the product puts on screen at once (Follower Bowling racks ten). The product page then tells a streamer with fewer how many slots are filled and that the rest fill in as followers arrive. Optional.

auto_play.description: A loop the installed product runs by itself: while the switch control is on and the list has people in it, the front of the list is popped every `seconds`, with nothing said in chat. The pop writes the same last_removed and last_removed_at the chat pop and draw actions write, so an overlay keyed on those needs no change. `list` is an installs.lists ref; `switch` is the key of a boolean control on one of the product's overlays; `seconds` must cover the overlay's animation for one item. Optional.

ready_message.description: One line for the moment every step is done, in the streamer's world: what their chat can do right now. Shown once, large, under 'Everything is in place'.

notes.description: Short plain-text lines shown on the product page after install, for the optional things the installer does not decide for the streamer.

highlights.description: Up to three short lines of what makes this product worth having, shown as ticked bullets beside its pitch on both the homepage teaser and the product's pitch page. Optional; a product without them shows its description alone.

pitch.description: The public product page, section by section. Only a listed `product` (not an `alert`) carries one, and ProductPitchPageTest requires it there. Text may wrap a command or a tag in backticks to set it in code type; nothing else is markup.

tagline.description: The page's H1: one line, what the product does on stream. Also the one-liner other product pages use to point at this one.

lede.description: Two or three sentences under the H1. No setup in it: the steps section says how.

plays.description: What chat does, as exactly three beats, each a picture, a short title and one line.

art.description: `chat`: a few chat lines, the last one highlighted. `stat`: one or two big values and a caption. `image`: a file under public/products/<slug>/.

plays_note.description: One quiet line under the three beats, optionally ending in a link to a named route.

reasons_heading.description: What the product is, plainly. Never pitched as making quiet viewers talk.

looks.description: Ways the product can look. Omit it and a product with a designer shows its designer presets instead; a product with neither has no looks section.

setup_note.description: One line under the setup steps. The steps themselves are derived from requires_bot.

faq.description: Questions about this product. Two shared ones (is it free, can I remove it) are added after these by the page.

closing.description: The headline beside the last Get button.

ingredients.description: The questions the install asks, in order. A recipe is a form, not a tree: each ingredient has fixed choices and a default, and an answer is written wherever the manifest or an overlay document says {{key}}. The answers are recorded on the instance, so the shipped files plus the answers always reproduce what was installed. Nothing here is an option set; those are Lists.

key.description: What a placeholder names: {{service}} is answered by the ingredient whose key is service.

question.description: The question as the install page asks it.

choices.description: The answers on offer. A value is what gets written into the placeholder; a label is what the person reads.

default.description: The value preselected on the install page and used when no answer is given. Must be one of the choices.

designer.description: The product's designer at /products/<slug>/design: knobs on the left, grouped by topic, the real overlay on the right, and one-click presets. Declaring this block is what gives a product the page; nothing else does. The knobs themselves are the overlay's own controls (label, type, bounds and choices all live on the control row), so this block only says how they are arranged and what the presets write. Every text, number, boolean and color control the overlay declares must appear in exactly one group, or be the skin_key; a control of any other type is not a designer knob and may not be grouped.

overlay.description: The ref of the overlay in installs.overlays whose controls the designer edits. One per product.

skin_key.description: The key of a text control rendered as a strip of buttons above the groups rather than a row in one: one button per preset, in preset order, and every preset's value for it must equal the preset's own key. Optional; a product with no such control simply has no strip.

groups.description: The sections down the left column, in order. Each names the control keys it holds, in the order they are rendered.

presets.description: The built-in looks, in the order the page offers them. A preset is a complete look: its values name every designer key (every grouped key plus the skin_key) and nothing else, and a value for a control with choices must be one of them. Which preset is active is never stored; it is derived by comparing the overlay's controls to each bundle.

extras.description: Account-level settings the page edits beside the knobs, and the sample feed. `sample_chat` puts the sample-chat rate, More and Clear above the preview (for an overlay that reads chat, which includes the emotes loop). `chat_window` is the chat foreach cap slider; `chat_filters` is the hide-commands switch and the hidden-chatters box. Each is a closed name the page knows.

stage.description: The OBS browser-source size the preview renders at, in pixels. The first entry with no `when` is the default; an entry with `when` applies while every named control holds the given value, and the last matching entry wins. Omitted, the preview is 1920 by 1080.

installs.description: Rows the installer creates in the account beyond the picker primitives: overlays from markdown files shipped next to the manifest, and integration connections. Everything here is idempotent per install and belongs to the instance.

overlays.description: Overlay documents to create, in the same markdown format the import button accepts and the public .md endpoint emits. Controls the document defines are created with it.

file.description: Filename relative to the manifest's directory. No path separators.

integrations.description: External service keys to connect on install, exactly as the service's settings page would: the integration row is created enabled and its controls are provisioned. An entry may be an ingredient placeholder, {{key}}, answered at install.

alert_triggers.description: Which events make an installed alert overlay fire, exactly as the Triggers tab saves them: one event_template_mappings row for Twitch, one external_event_template_mappings row otherwise. The install refuses if the account already has an alert on the same event, because claiming it would silently stop the streamer's own alert firing.

overlay.description: The ref of an overlay declared in installs.overlays. Its document must be type: alert.

service.description: "twitch" for an EventSub event, otherwise an external service key registered in ExternalServiceRegistry. May be an ingredient placeholder, {{key}}, answered at install.

event_type.description: An event type from EventTemplateMapping::EVENT_TYPES when service is twitch, otherwise one from ExternalEventTemplateMapping::SERVICE_EVENT_TYPES for that service.

duration_ms.description: How long the alert stays on screen. Matches the column default when omitted.

alert_targets.description: Which installed static overlays an installed alert fires on, the alert_template_static_overlays pivot the Targeting tab writes. Declaring nothing leaves the alert firing on every static overlay, which is the platform default.

alert.description: The ref of an overlay declared in installs.overlays. Its document must be type: alert.

overlays.description: Refs of overlays declared in installs.overlays. Each document must be type: static.

lists.description: User Lists to create, empty, exactly as /lists creates one. The slug is what the overlay's [[[c:list:<slug>]]] tags and the !list command name, so it is fixed by the manifest, not per instance. The install refuses if the account already has a list with that slug.

list_appenders.description: Chat commands that append to one of the lists above, exactly as the list's Appenders panel creates one. The install refuses if the command name is already taken on the account.

list.description: The ref of a list declared in installs.lists.

value.description: What gets appended. Defaults to the chatter's name, [[[bot:from_user]]].

bot_aliases.description: Bot Aliases to create, exactly as /settings/bot/aliases creates one: a short command that the bot expands to a longer one. The streamer can rename or delete them afterwards. Validated by BotAliasValidator, so the same rules apply as in the form (no chains, no self-loops, {1}/{*} placeholders only).

target.description: What the bot runs instead, e.g. '!list lane pop first'.

bot_commands.description: Custom Bot Commands to create, exactly as /settings/bot/commands creates one. Validated by BotCommandValidator, so the reply obeys the same rules as in the form, and any counter: tag it names is provisioned.

reply.description: The templated text the bot speaks.

option_sets.description: Named, reusable lists of values that pickers draw from.

pickers.description: RNG / selection engines over an option set.

control_exports.description: Maps picker state to user-facing controls. Each export becomes a [[[c:<slug>:<instance>:<name>]]] tag at install time.

triggers.description: Entry points that fire pickers (chat command, dashboard button). EventSub and scheduled triggers are deliberately out of v1.

primitiveRef.description: Manifest-local identifier for a primitive. Translated to a real DB id and per-instance slug at install time.

controlExportName.description: Name of an exported control. Lands as the third colon segment in the tag namespace.

items.description: Default items. Each item is a short string. User-editable option sets accept post-install edits within min/max bounds.

option_set_ref.description: Must match the ref of an option_set declared in the same manifest.

from.description: Dotted path to the picker state being exported. Currently only pickers.<ref>.{result|result_at|running} are supported.

fires.description: Dotted path to the picker that fires. Format: pickers.<ref>.
